items.name: Celluloid
items.description: Celluloid plays local video and audio through mpv. It is part of the curated Vital OS set. The catalog icon is original.

items.name: Firefox
items.summary: Web browser from Mozilla's apt archive.
items.description: Firefox is already part of the Vital OS image, installed from packages.mozilla.org rather than a snap. Marketplace can reinstall it with apt if it has been removed. The icon in this catalog is an original Vital tile, not the Firefox logo.

items.name: GIMP
items.description: GNU Image Manipulation Program. Vital Marketplace installs the Flathub build org.gimp.GIMP. Flathub must be reachable the first time. The catalog icon is an original tile, not the GIMP mascot.

items.name: Inkscape
items.description: Inkscape edits SVG drawings. Vital Marketplace installs org.inkscape.Inkscape from Flathub. The catalog icon is original.

items.name: Vital Assistant
items.summary: System-wide assistant. Nothing changes until you confirm.
items.description: Vital Assistant 0.3.0 is one per-user daemon shared by the terminal, a Super+Space overlay, and Settings. The default provider is xAI Grok with your own key from console.x.ai, stored in the system keyring and never written to a file or sent to vital-os.org. OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Ollama, and an optional local llama.cpp model are also supported. If the network is down or no key is stored, a ready local model answers instead, and the reply says which provider spoke. System actions are an allowlist (GNOME settings, open a known app, search or install through Marketplace, apt, or Flatpak, and disk, update, battery, and network status). State-changing actions show the exact command and wait. Privileged installs go through polkit. There is no root shell. Context from files, the active window, the clipboard, or a screenshot is off until you turn it on for that question. Hebrew and English are included. Prompts are not telemetry. This package is installed on the image. Marketplace can update it after the SHA-256 matches.

items.name: Vital Example Note
items.summary: Example script. It prints one line and changes nothing.
items.description: This entry exists so the script installer can be reviewed. It is not a product. Marketplace shows the script and asks before it runs. The helper downloads it again and refuses it if the SHA-256 does not match. A .deb would use the same url and sha256 fields with method deb.

items.name: Vital Local Model
items.summary: Offline Qwen3 0.6B and llama.cpp for Vital Assistant.
items.description: Optional local provider for Vital Assistant. The script downloads two pinned files and checks SHA-256 before it installs them. The model is the official Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-GGUF file Qwen3-0.6B-Q8_0.gguf (639446688 bytes, SHA-256 9465e63a22add5354d9bb4b99e90117043c7124007664907259bd16d043bb031), Apache-2.0. On 2026-11-09 that repository published this Q8_0 file and no Q4_K_M file. The runtime is llama.cpp b12212 (MIT): llama-b12212-bin-ubuntu-x64.tar.gz (SHA-256 a9b987738e6724b116980de8f5e15a901a3086587c3d2328533d77582e25ad5b). A Vulkan build (SHA-256 1f4c94a3a38b52ed632924aba9cdfa736caaa3ea7812b62ca1d8b84917eb3e15) is added only when /dev/dri/renderD128 exists. CPU is the default. The assistant listens on 127.0.0.1. This does not collect telemetry.
